title: A pilot who logs two flights on the same aircraft while offline always gets the second one held for review, so aircraft totals omit it until an administrator acts
steps: 1. Open the demo, let the service worker install, go offline. 2. Flight log > Log a completed flight on N206MA: time 2 h ago, ending Hobbs 2342.2, save. 3. Log a second flight on N206MA: time 30 min ago, ending Hobbs 2343.0, save. (The second form still shows starting Hobbs 2,341.2, the pre-first-leg value.) 4. Go online and let both entries sync.
expected: Both legs are accepted in order (same author, same device, strictly increasing times and readings) and the aircraft Hobbs is 2,343.0; or the second entry is stamped with the version it will see after the first one syncs.
actual: Leg 1 is accepted. Leg 2 is stored as Needs review with reason "Aircraft totals changed after this entry was started." Aircraft Hobbs stays 2,342.2 and every hours-based due figure is 0.8 h behind until an administrator reviews it. Every further offline leg is held the same way.
evidence: shots/flights-offline-two-legs.png; script output: flight2: review 'Aircraft totals changed after this entry was started.'; src/components/FlightForm.tsx:764 (baseVersion: m.opening.version, taken from the cached snapshot, which enqueue() never advances); src/domain/flights.ts:190
suspect: src/components/FlightForm.tsx:764 with src/data/store.ts:349-410 (enqueue does not account for the author's own pending flights on the same aircraft) and src/domain/flights.ts:190
notes: The server runs the same conflictReason (convex/operations.ts submit -> submitOperation), so the live app behaves the same: op.baseVersion is the version cached before leg 1. README 'Offline and installation' promises only that 'conflicting flights' go to review; a pilot's own consecutive legs are not a conflict. Multi-leg days without signal are the normal case for a mission program. The same applies to the logbook import when more than one row targets an aircraft only if the import stamps one version (not checked here).

title: The server refuses a queued flight with a plain Error for a removed or inactive crew member, a fast device clock or a missing meter reading, so in production the Sync center shows only "Something went wrong" instead of the reason docs/offline.md promises (the demo shows the reason)
steps: 1. Copy repro/flights/zz-hunt-flights-refusal-text.test.ts to convex/. 2. Run `npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-flights-refusal-text.test.ts`. 3. Each case submits a flight through api.operations.submit: (a) copilot who is no longer in the program, (b) copilot deactivated, (c) start time 10 minutes ahead of the server clock, (d) no reading for the aircraft's meter.
expected: Each refusal is a ConvexError carrying its message ("Pilot must belong to this Flight Program.", "Select an active copilot.", "Flight time cannot be in the future.", "The hobbs reading is required for this aircraft."), so the entry shows it under Needs attention; docs/offline.md line 9 names "a pilot no longer in the program" as an entry that 'stays in the Sync center as Needs attention with the server's reason'.
actual: All four are plain Error. submit exposes only FlightRejection (convex/operations.ts:155), and production Convex replaces any other error with "Server Error"; store.ts treats the "[CONVEX …" message as permanent and errorText() stores the generic "Something went wrong. Try again, and tell an administrator if it keeps happening." The pilot cannot tell what to edit before Edit and retry. The demo wraps every error in a ConvexError (demoBackend.ts:160-168), so the demo shows the real reason and hides the gap.
evidence: vitest output: 4 failed, e.g. 'expected Error: Flight time cannot be in the futur… to match object { name: ConvexError }'; src/domain/flightSubmission.ts:236-253 (plain Error), src/domain/flights.ts:164-171 (comment claims a plain Error is retried; convex/outboxRefusals.test.ts:163-175 shows a plain server Error is in fact held with the generic text); src/data/errors.ts:44-47
suspect: convex/operations.ts:155 (expose: errorsOf(FlightRejection)) with src/domain/flightSubmission.ts:203-253 and src/domain/flights.ts:164-171
notes: The clock-skew case needs no user error: the phone's start time is 'now' on a clock >5 min fast. The same applies to 'Aircraft not found.', 'Entry ID already used.' and the checklist/plan refusals if they are plain Errors (not checked one by one). The comment at flights.ts:164-166 is wrong for the live path: a server-side plain Error is not retried, it is held with the generic text.

title: Stale-save review on the AD form: "Keep mine" puts a required action's next-due limit back to its value from before the other person's compliance (or due-limit edit), and the review shows the two copies of "Required actions" as identical text
steps: 1. Demo, Airworthiness: Add AD 2026-01-01, Applicable, one Recurring action, next due 2300 h, repeat 100 h; save. 2. Open Details > Review / edit AD, change the Subject (give a reason), leave the form open. 3. In a second tab of the same browser open the same AD and Record compliance at 2340 h (next due becomes 2440 h). 4. Back in the first tab press Save AD; the review 'Someone else changed this AD' opens. 5. Press Keep mine.
expected: The review shows what differs in the required actions (next due 2300 h vs 2440 h) and marks who changed what, so the user can decide; a change the user did not make (the due limits moved by compliance) is not undone without being shown. The compliance history row should not be offered as a field 'Keep mine' will replace, or should be readable.
actual: The review lists FAA SOURCE (correct), REQUIRED ACTIONS with the same text on both sides ('Inspect fittings per paragraph (g)' | 'Inspect fittings per paragraph (g)'), and HISTORY as raw JSON ('[]' vs the full compliance object), with no 'Changed by' markers (the AD form passes no loaded copy). The footer says 'Keep mine saves your values for every field above'. After Keep mine the AD is at version 3 with the compliance entry kept (server restores history) but tasks[0].dueHours back at 2300: the AD reads overdue at 2340 h although compliance was just recorded, and in the opposite case (the other person corrected a due limit downward) Keep mine silently restores the later, wrong limit.
evidence: shots/flights-stale-ad-review.png; script output 'after their compliance: dueHours 2440 ... after Keep mine: dueHours 2300, history 1'; src/components/Airworthiness.tsx:1100-1118 (formatADTasks prints descriptions only; no spec for history), :1164-1170 (attempt has no `loaded`); src/domain/airworthiness.ts:771-781 (saveAD keeps old.history but takes tasks from the draft); src/domain/fieldDiff.ts:135-139 (nested values compare by JSON, so the row appears, but its text hides the difference)
notes: Reproduced in the demo; the server runs the same applyADCommand (convex/airworthiness.ts:36) so the stored result is the same. docs/offline.md says each field is 'marked as changed by you, by them or by both': the AD form shows no markers. The work order form formats its tasks the same way (WorkOrders.tsx:734-736: descriptions only), see FL-4 if recorded.

title: "Edit and retry" on a refused flight drops the discrepancy the pilot wrote on it: the retry form opens with the Discrepancy box empty and the saved entry files no problem report
steps: 1. Demo, wait for the service worker, go offline. 2. Discrepancies > Report a problem on N206MA, tick 'Aircraft not airworthy', save (this grounds the aircraft once synced). 3. Overview > Log a flight on N206MA: ending Hobbs 2342.2, time 2026-01-01 10:00, Remarks 'Night leg, crosswind landing', Discrepancy 'Left brake pedal soft on rollout'; save. 4. Go online. The flight is refused at the dispatch gate and shows Needs attention in the Sync center. 5. Press Edit and retry. 6. Enter the administrator override reason and Save flight.
expected: The retry form is 'prefilled from the entry' (docs/offline.md): the Discrepancy box holds 'Left brake pedal soft on rollout', and the retried flight creates the linked open problem report.
actual: Remarks are prefilled but the Discrepancy box is empty. The new entry replaces the failed one, syncs as accepted with discrepancy "", and no report about the brake exists anywhere; the failed entry (the only copy of the text) has been discarded from the device by replace().
evidence: shots/flights-edit-retry-discrepancy.png; script output: retry form: remarks = "Night leg, crosswind landing" discrepancy = ""; synced flight discrepancy: "" ... reports about the brake: 0. src/components/FlightForm.tsx:685-690 (the discrepancy textarea has no defaultValue, unlike Remarks at :653-656) and :807 (discrepancy: initial?.discrepancy ?? value(data, 'discrepancy'))
notes: New with the Edit and retry feature merged on 9 Nov (fc55ad8). tests/e2e/stale-save.spec.ts covers Edit and retry only for a flight without a discrepancy. The data layer is the same in the live app (store.replace discards the old entry after enqueue succeeds), so this is not demo-only.

title: A pilot who started a flight on an airworthy aircraft cannot end (log) it once a grounding problem is reported, including the pilot's own report after landing: the End flight form is fully disabled and the flown hours stay unlogged
steps: 1. Demo as a line pilot (the repro moves the demo user into the demo 'Pilots' group: read, flight, discrepancy). 2. Flight log > Start flight on N206MA: tick both verifications, fill preflight, Save preflight & start flight. 3. After 'landing', Discrepancies > Report a problem on N206MA, tick 'Aircraft not airworthy', save. 4. Flight log > End flight.
expected: A flight that was released while the aircraft was airworthy and has already been flown can be completed by its pilot (the dispatch gate was passed at Start flight), or at least the readings can be entered and saved for an administrator to accept, so the hours, landings and cycles reach the record.
actual: The End flight dialog shows 'N206MA is grounded. Flights cannot be logged until these items are resolved or deferred' and every field and 'End flight & save' are disabled. The pilot cannot record the closing readings at all; only an administrator can log the flight (with a dispatch override worded as if the flight had not happened yet). Until then aircraft total time, landings and cycles omit a flight that took place.
evidence: shots/flights-session-grounded.png; script output 'Ending Hobbs field disabled: true ... End flight & save disabled: true'; src/components/FlightForm.tsx:728-735 (saveBlocked applies to every phase) and :250 (gated = !initial && !!aircraft, phase not considered); src/data/store.ts:376-381 and src/domain/flightSubmission.ts:109 (the gate runs again at enqueue and at sync, against the state at logging time, not at the flight's start)
notes: The natural order after a bad landing is 'report the problem, then finish the paperwork'. The same gate refuses an offline 'Log a completed flight' that syncs after someone else grounded the aircraft (docs/offline.md calls that 'a dispatch gate it cannot pass'); that case at least leaves the entry in the Sync center. Here nothing is saved. Owner decision: whether the gate should judge the aircraft at the flight's start time, or let the pilot save a held entry.

title: A problem report filed through the flight form's Discrepancy box is created with no change-log row of its own (a standalone report writes discrepancy.created)
steps: 1. Copy repro/flights/zz-hunt-flights-report-audit.test.ts to convex/. 2. Run `npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-flights-report-audit.test.ts` (test 'FL-6'). It submits a flight whose discrepancy is 'Left brake pedal soft on rollout' through api.operations.submit, then reads the discrepancies and audit tables.
expected: The new open report '<flight uuid>-discrepancy' has a 'discrepancy.created' audit row under its own entity id, like a report filed from Discrepancies > Report a problem (flightSubmission.ts:170-180), so its history starts with its creation and the 'Changes by person' counts include it.
actual: The report row exists (status open) but the audit table holds no row with entityUuid '<flight uuid>-discrepancy'. The only trace is the text inside the flight.created (or flight.held) row's 'after' payload under the flight's id. Later rows for the report (deferred, parts, resolved) therefore have no creation row before them.
evidence: vitest: 'FL-6 ... AssertionError: expected [] to include discrepancy.created'; src/domain/flightSubmission.ts:293-326 (listFlightAudit: stock, flight, override; nothing for the report) vs :165-181; convex/operations.ts:678-679 inserts the report
notes: Same in the demo (shared submitOperation). A held or later rejected flight still files the report, so the report can outlive any accepted flight row; its origin is then only findable through the held flight's payload.

title: operations.submit answers "accepted" to a resent entry id whose contents differ from the stored flight; the device then deletes the entry although none of the new readings were stored
steps: 1. Copy repro/flights/zz-hunt-flights-report-audit.test.ts to convex/. 2. Run `npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-flights-report-audit.test.ts` (test 'FL-7'). It submits a flight, then submits the same uuid again with a different ending Hobbs and landings.
expected: A repeat with identical contents returns the stored status (idempotent retry). A repeat whose contents differ is refused (as runCommand does for other commands: 'Request identifier already used.') or stored, so the device does not drop an entry the server ignored.
actual: The second call returns { status: 'accepted' }; the stored flight keeps the first readings. store.ts flushPass removes the outbox entry and shows 'Entry synchronized successfully.'
evidence: vitest: 'FL-7 ... expected false to be true'; src/domain/flightSubmission.ts:103-104 and :187-194 (resubmitted checks only the author); convex/operations.ts:555-564; src/data/store.ts:536-543
notes: Reachability in the UI is narrow: Start flight/End flight and the guided flight reuse one id per session (FlightSession.tsx:562, GuidedFlight.tsx:962), so it needs the tab to close between enqueue and the session being cleared, then End flight again with other readings. Edit and retry uses a new id. Related known item LO-1 is the inspection form, where the edited retry is refused rather than silently accepted.

title: Stale-save review on the work order form: "Keep mine" reverts a task status and parts-delay note that a mechanic saved meanwhile, and the review shows "Requested work" with identical text on both sides
steps: 1. Demo, Work orders: Open work order WO-STALE-1 with one requested work item 'Inspect cabin fittings'. 2. Open its Details, change Assigned supervisor, leave the form open. 3. In a second tab open the same order, expand Task 1, set status 'parts-delay' with the note 'Awaiting replacement fitting', Save work order. 4. In the first tab press Save work order; the review 'Someone else changed this work order' opens. 5. Press Keep mine.
expected: The review shows what differs inside the tasks (Task 1 status requested vs parts-delay, the delay note), and a supervisor edit does not undo task progress the user never touched; or Keep mine is refused when it would revert task state.
actual: The review lists SUPERVISOR (changed by you) and REQUESTED WORK (changed by them) with 'Inspect cabin fittings' on both sides. After Keep mine the order is at version 3 with Task 1 status back to 'requested' and partsDelay ''. The mechanic's entry survives only in the change log. The same path reverts a task marked completed, its notes and work-performed text.
evidence: shots/flights-stale-workorder-review.png; script output: after their save status parts-delay / partsDelay 'Awaiting replacement fitting'; rows [[SUPERVISOR CHANGED BY YOU, Second supervisor, First supervisor],[REQUESTED WORK CHANGED BY THEM, Inspect cabin fittings, Inspect cabin fittings]]; after Keep mine status requested, partsDelay ''. src/components/WorkOrders.tsx:734-736 (formatTasks prints descriptions only), :1141-1148 (draft and save both send draft.tasks, the tasks as loaded), src/domain/workOrders.ts:581-618 (save replaces the task list)
repro: repro/flights/stale-workorder-keep-mine.js (argument 'theirs' or 'cancel' drives the other two choices; both behave as documented)
notes: Same class as FL-3 (AD form). Demo and server share saveWorkOrder, so the stored result is the same live. Use theirs reloaded the form with the stored supervisor and task status; Cancel kept the draft and stored nothing.

title: A device clock that runs behind the server locks the user out right after sign-in with "Your seven-day offline access has expired", and blocks queuing and sync, until the device clock passes the sign-in time
steps: 1. `node repro/flights/access-window-probe.js skew`: opens the demo, sets the cached snapshot's authenticatedAt to 3 minutes after the device's current time (what a server whose clock is 3 minutes ahead of the phone stamps on a fresh session), and reloads. 2. Read the screen.
expected: A freshly signed-in user opens the workspace. A small clock difference is tolerated, as the flight rules already do for start times (FUTURE_START_TOLERANCE_MS = 5 min, src/domain/flights.ts:26).
actual: The app shows 'Time to reconnect. Your seven-day offline access has expired. Pending entries are preserved. Sign in again to continue.' offlineValid requires now >= authenticatedAt with no tolerance; authenticatedAt is the server's session creation time (convex/operations.ts:331) and now is the device clock (src/main.tsx:359). The gate rechecks every 15 s, so the lockout lasts as long as the clock difference (permanently for a clock set to the wrong day). During it enqueue() refuses new entries and canFlush() stops sync (store.ts:351, :209). 'Return to sign in' signs the user out, and signing in again gives the same screen.
evidence: shots/flights-clock-behind-lockout.png; script output 'REPRODUCED: a session stamped 3 minutes ahead of the device clock opens on "Time to reconnect."'; src/domain/model.ts:442-448
repro: repro/flights/access-window-probe.js (argument 'skew'; with 'all' it prints the day 6/7/8 behaviour, which is as documented)
notes: Reproduced in the demo by stamping the snapshot; the live path uses the same offlineValid with a server-side timestamp, so only the size of the real clock difference is assumed. The message is also wrong for this case (nothing expired). The window itself held: valid at 6 days and at 7 days minus a minute, expired at exactly 7 and at 8 days; a flight queued before expiry stayed on the device, did not sync while expired even when online, and synced after renewal by the same account.

title: Stale-save review on the inspection form shows "Due at (hours)" as "—" for my copy and marks it "Changed by both" although I did not touch it and Keep mine saves 2,400.0; required parts are printed as raw JSON
steps: 1. `node repro/flights/stale-inspection-probe.js`: creates inspection TEST-STALE (repeat 100 h, last complied 2300 h), opens Inspection details and rewords the Description, then writes 'someone else's' save into the stored record (last complied 2340 h, due 2440 h, materials, a calendar exemption, one required part; version + 1) and presses Save inspection. 2. Read the review rows, press Keep mine, read the stored record.
expected: Each row shows the value Keep mine will store; a field the user did not edit is marked 'Changed by them'; lists are shown readably.
actual: Row 'DUE AT (HOURS) / CHANGED BY BOTH: — | 2,440.0', but after Keep mine dueSeconds is 8640000 (2,400.0 h, recomputed from the interval), not blank. Row 'REQUIRED PARTS: [] | [{"uuid":"1111…","partNumber":"MS-1",…}]' is raw JSON. All other fields the other person changed (materials, calendar exemption and reason, last complied hours and date) are listed honestly as 'Changed by them' and are overwritten by Keep mine, as docs/offline.md states.
evidence: script output (rows and 'after Keep mine' record); src/components/Management.tsx:1013 (dueSeconds read from a blank form field), :854 (no format for requiredParts); src/domain/fieldDiff.ts:102-108
repro: repro/flights/stale-inspection-probe.js (prints the rows; it is a probe, not a pass/fail script)
notes: On this form Keep mine is a documented whole-record overwrite and the review is otherwise honest, unlike the AD and work order forms (FL-3, FL-8). Note the consequence still shown only as numbers: if the other save was a recorded completion, Keep mine puts last-complied and due back to the pre-completion values.

title: Server proof for FL-3: a re-save of an AD draft loaded before a compliance is accepted by api.airworthiness.save at the current version, moves next due from 2440 h back to 2300 h, and logs that under the user's unrelated reason
steps: 1. Copy repro/flights/zz-hunt-flights-keep-mine-ad.test.ts to convex/. 2. Run `npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-flights-keep-mine-ad.test.ts`.
expected: The stored action keeps dueHours 2440 after the subject-only edit (the test asserts this and fails today).
actual: Stored dueHours is 2300 with the compliance entry still in history. The change log holds three rows for the AD: ad.save (after 2300), ad.comply (2300 -> 2440), ad.save with reason 'Subject wording corrected.' (before 2440, after 2300). So both versions are recorded, but the due-limit reversal carries a reason about the subject wording.
evidence: vitest output (console 'audit rows' and 'expected 2300 to be 2440'); src/domain/airworthiness.ts:771-781
notes: Supporting evidence, not a separate defect: count it with FL-3. It answers 'does the audit row record both versions': yes, before and after are both stored on every save.

title: FL-2 has one more user-reachable sibling: a guided flight whose checklist was removed or moved while the entry waited is refused with a plain Error ("Checklist is unavailable for this aircraft or Flight Program."), shown in production as "Something went wrong"
steps: 1. Copy repro/flights/zz-hunt-flights-refusal-text.test.ts to convex/. 2. Run `npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-flights-refusal-text.test.ts`; the fifth case submits a flight whose checklistRun names a checklist the server does not hold.
expected: A ConvexError carrying 'Checklist is unavailable for this aircraft or Flight Program.' so the Sync center shows it.
actual: A plain Error (src/domain/flightChecklistLink.ts:36-41), not exposed by submit's errorsOf(FlightRejection).
evidence: vitest: 'a guided flight whose checklist was removed while the entry waited ... expected Error: Checklist is unavailable … to match object { name: ConvexError }'
notes: Fix with FL-2. Survey of the other flight-line paths (by reading, 10 Nov): flight plans and checklists refuse with Rejection (always exposed by runCommand), except checklists.ts:260 'A checklist cannot change Flight Program.' (plain; needs a forged or stale program id). Plain and not reachable from the UI as far as I could see: 'Aircraft not found.', 'Entry ID already used.', 'Linked flight does not belong to this aircraft.' (flightSubmission.ts:107,192,200), 'Report not found.' and 'This offline entry belongs to a different user. Sign in with the original account.' (convex/operations.ts:701,545; the outbox filters by author before sending). A ZodError on submit is also hidden (pinned as current behaviour at convex/operations.test.ts:358); the device parses the same schema in enqueue first.
